report.source_text: Upon admission, laboratory tests showed: urinary protein 4+, red blood cells 71.9/uL, white blood cells 1.8/uL; 24-hour urine protein 4.5 g; serum albumin 16.5 g/l; serum creatinine 63 µmol/L (corresponding to an estimated glomerular filtration rate of 123 mL/min/1.73 m² as calculated by the CKD-EPI equation); hemoglobin 115 g/L; white blood cell counts 3.68 × 10^9/L; mature lymphocyte counts 0.81 × 10^9/L; platelets were normal. CD4 + T cell counts: 77/Ul (reference range, 441–2156/uL); CD8 + T cell counts: 339/uL (reference range,125–1312/uL); CD4/CD8+: 0.23 (reference range, 0.71–2.78); NK cell counts 49/uL (reference range, 95–640/uL). TSH: 24.90 mIU/L, FT3: 3.44pmol/L, TT4: 53.80nmol/L, thyroglobulin: 52.40ng/Ml. Anti-nuclear antibody 1:100, anti-double-stranded DNA antibody with titer of 25.4/IU. All extractable nuclear antigen (ENA) test were negative. The complement C3 levels were reduced to 0.58 g/L, while complement C4 0.17 g/L was within the normal range. Subsequent investigations disclosed that the serum immunoglobulin G (IgG) concentration was markedly diminished, registering at 4.51 g/L. The assays for anti-neutrophil cytoplasmic antibody (ANCA), anti-glomerular basement membrane (GBM) antibody, serum anti-M-type phospholipase A2 receptor (PLA2R) antibody, Coombs’test, antiphospholipid antibody, immunofixation electrophoresis, and tumor biomarkers all manifested negative findings. The viral serological screenings for herpes simplex virus (HSV) and rubella virus (RV) exhibited equivocal results. The diagnostic tests for hepatitis B virus, hepatitis C virus, Epstein-Barr virus (EBV), cytomegalovirus (CMV), syphilis, and HIV were all negative. Bone marrow flow cytometry analysis did not identify any conspicuous aberrant hematopoietic lymphocytes and plasma cells. Whole-genome sequencing failed to detect any genetic polymorphisms or mutations.

clinician.final_diagnosis: ICL (Inborn Errors of Immunity) and Class V lupus nephritis
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 35-year-old Chinese male chef presented with six months of persistent foamuria, progressive generalized edema, and scattered verrucous hyperplasia. Initial workup revealed nephrotic range proteinuria (24-hour urine protein 4.5g, urinary protein 4+, serum albumin 16.5 g/L), hematuria (RBC 71.9/uL), and normal serum creatinine. Autoimmune serology showed positive ANA (1:100), positive anti-dsDNA (25.4/IU), and reduced C3 (0.58 g/L), with normal C4. A pathological diagnosis of Class V lupus nephritis was made. Further immunological investigation revealed severe lymphopenia (CD4+ T cells 77/uL, CD8+ T cells 339/uL, NK cells 49/uL) and markedly diminished serum IgG (4.51 g/L). Whole-genome sequencing did not detect genetic mutations. During one-year follow-up, the patient experienced deep vein embolism, acute kidney injury, and cytomegaloviraemia, with persistent proteinuria and worsening verrucous lesions.

Pathological diagnosis confirmed Class V lupus nephritis.
